description: Baseline P0-P3 acceptance scan; existing migration snapshot ancestry check fails before implementation changes.

asi.hypothesis: Establish objective baseline before implementing roadmap gates.
asi.rollback_reason: Repository baseline contract suite has a migration snapshot ancestry mismatch unrelated to the new autoresearch harness.
asi.next_action_hint: Diagnose and repair the existing migration snapshot chain first so later improvements can be kept.

description: Reconciled order confirmation with ADR-0033 and repaired migration ancestry; process PostgreSQL tests exposed an accounting period date bug.

asi.hypothesis: Server-derived order lines and accounting profiles will close the ADR-0033 reconciliation gate.
asi.rollback_reason: Accounting period lookup still reports closed despite an open 2000-2099 period; changes reverted by experiment harness.
asi.next_action_hint: Fix utcDate: tests run with the Effect test clock at epoch, so posting date resolves to 1970-01-01. Use a provided current date/test clock or open period covering epoch in process tests, then reapply the captured ADR-0033 diff.
asi.learned: The production service uses Clock.Clock, and @effect/vitest supplies a test clock unless explicitly live; date-sensitive PostgreSQL tests must control/provide clock intentionally.

description: Align order confirmation with ADR-0033 and repair the migration snapshot ancestry chain.

asi.hypothesis: Server-derived order lines and accounting posting close the superseded workflow gap without broadening architecture.
asi.result: Process now reserves Sales-owned lines, derives revenue from order total, and no longer accepts client journal facts; tests and repository checks pass.
asi.test_clock_note: Date-sensitive @effect/vitest integration fixtures cover the epoch-based test clock explicitly.

description: Reconciled P0 and roadmap wording, but the current coarse metric already counted the conditional P0 readiness sentence.

asi.hypothesis: Explicit P0 closure and roadmap reconciliation would close an uncounted acceptance gate.
asi.rollback_reason: No primary metric improvement because the harness's P0 grep already treated 'P0 is READY only when...' as closure.
asi.next_action_hint: Bundle these documentation corrections with the next substantive P1 improvement, and later tighten the harness wording check without claiming a standalone gain.
asi.useful_changes: P0 explicit READY status; fiscal periods PARTIAL; process distinguished from Process Studio.

description: Accept the P1 inventory primitive baseline and reconcile P0/roadmap status.

asi.hypothesis: A narrow discrete-stock baseline resolves P1 without speculative conversion, traceability, valuation, or location hierarchy.
asi.result: ADR-0035 defines Item UOM, whole quantities, warehouse location, non-negative stock, append-only correction, and explicit non-goals; P0 is explicitly closed and roadmap drift is corrected.
asi.deferred: Implementation of UOM DTOs and idempotent correction command remains the next gate.

description: Implemented P1 UOM and correction semantics; one PostgreSQL assertion still queried the removed enum value.

asi.hypothesis: An idempotent signed adjustment command plus immutable item UOM closes the P1 implementation gate.
asi.rollback_reason: The integration test counted corrections with kind='adjustment' after implementation intentionally encoded correction direction as existing receipt/issue kinds to avoid unsafe same-transaction enum evolution.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply/retain the P1 patch and change the movement-count assertion to filter by correction idempotency key or non-null correction metadata, then rerun.
asi.migration_learning: Using existing receipt/issue direction plus correction metadata avoids PostgreSQL's unsafe-use-of-new-enum-value migration failure.

description: Implement immutable Item UOM and idempotent append-oriented stock corrections for the P1 baseline.

asi.hypothesis: A single-unit discrete-stock contract and signed idempotent correction command provide the minimum executable P1 proof.
asi.result: Inventory now defaults/normalizes UOM, validates correction units, serializes negative corrections against reserved stock, and preserves correction history with tenant-scoped idempotency.
asi.validation: Inventory unit/PostgreSQL tests, migration catalog, db check, boundary lint, type check, and contract checks passed.
asi.migration_design: Corrections reuse receipt/issue movement direction plus correction metadata, avoiding a PostgreSQL enum migration transaction hazard.

description: Define and enforce the P2 document, fixed-scale money, revenue period, and reversal baseline.

asi.hypothesis: Owner-local documents plus a fixed two-decimal Legal Entity posting baseline resolve P2 without inventing invoice, payment, tax, or settlement policy.
asi.result: ADR-0036 establishes document/correction ownership; accounting now enforces precision 2 at Schema and PostgreSQL boundaries with open/closed-period and idempotent reversal proofs.
asi.validation: Focused accounting contract/PostgreSQL tests, migration checks, boundary checks, type checks, and repository contract checks passed.
asi.explicit_non_goals: Tax, AP/AR, invoices, payments, settlement, reopen, adjusting periods, FX, and multi-currency remain unpublished until separately decided.

description: Define the P3 boundary and add neutral typed catalog contracts with Inventory and Accounting contributors.

asi.hypothesis: A contract-only catalog leaf plus domain-owned declarations resolves catalog ownership without coupling domains to Process Studio.
asi.result: ADR-0037 distinguishes business audit authority, declarations, aggregation, delivery intent, receipts, PgQue gates, and external adapters; Inventory and Accounting action/event schemas now have compatibility tests.
asi.current_limit: Domain events remain EXPERIMENTAL until owner-controlled transaction-aware publication exists; Process event was renamed to process.order_confirmation.completed to stop coordinator impersonation.
asi.validation: Catalog compatibility, boundary, type, and contract checks passed.

description: Complete the initial P0-P3 acceptance portfolio with explicit period-close concurrency evidence.

asi.hypothesis: The existing close/post race test is the concrete P2 transactional-period proof; naming it explicitly makes the acceptance harness reflect the real evidence.
asi.result: All ten initial acceptance gates now pass with repository correctness checks.
asi.important_remaining_work: Do not stop: P3 events are still EXPERIMENTAL, owner-controlled transaction-aware publication and durable completed consumer receipts remain to implement before claiming P3 READY.

name: Close EclipseERP P3 and ADR-0033 runtime gaps

description: Baseline remaining P3 and ADR-0033 runtime readiness gaps.

asi.hypothesis: Re-baseline after completing the initial P0-P3 decision portfolio.
asi.result: None of the seven stricter runtime-readiness gates pass yet.
asi.harness_issue: The P3 READY grep used backticks inside double quotes and emitted a harmless shell substitution error; fix before next run.

description: Add the transaction-aware internal messaging outbox and completed consumer receipt foundation.

asi.hypothesis: A dedicated messaging infrastructure package can own event envelopes and duplicate-safe local consumption without owning business event meaning.
asi.result: Messaging now appends idempotent typed envelopes and commits PostgreSQL-local consumer effects with completed receipts in one transaction; duplicate and rollback tests pass.
asi.scope_boundary: consumeOnce explicitly excludes external exactly-once claims; provider effects still require provider idempotency and outcome reconciliation.
asi.validation: Focused unit/PostgreSQL tests, migrations, DB check, boundary lint, type check, and contract checks passed.

description: Route Process-owned lifecycle events through Messaging with distinct command, correlation, causation, and idempotency metadata.

asi.hypothesis: Replacing direct outbox writes with the public MessagingService preserves the shared transaction while separating execution identities.
asi.result: Order confirmation appends a Process-owned event through Messaging; API composition and PostgreSQL tests verify distinct metadata and the messaging outbox.
asi.validation: Full type, contract, boundary, and test checks passed.

description: Publish Inventory stock correction events atomically from the owning command path.

asi.hypothesis: Injecting MessagingService into Inventory lets stock correction and its owner event commit or roll back together without domain access to messaging tables.
asi.result: adjustStock now carries distinct execution identities, emits one PUBLIC inventory.stock.corrected event on creation, skips publication on idempotent replay, and rolls back balance/movement when append fails.
asi.validation: Atomic publication, idempotency, rollback, catalog compatibility, type, contract, and boundary checks passed.

description: Publish Accounting revenue-posted events atomically from the owning command path.

asi.hypothesis: Mirroring Inventory's transaction-aware publication lets Accounting own a process-safe revenue event without coordinator impersonation.
asi.result: postRevenueForOrder carries distinct execution identities, emits one PUBLIC accounting.revenue.posted event only on creation, and rolls back journal lines when append fails.
asi.validation: Accounting unit/PostgreSQL atomic publication tests, process/bootstrap integration, catalog compatibility, type, contract, and boundary checks passed.

description: Make the durable duplicate-event and consumer-receipt rollback proofs explicit.

asi.hypothesis: The messaging implementation already satisfies the receipt gate; explicit test names should make the proof discoverable without changing semantics.
asi.result: Unit and PostgreSQL tests now clearly identify duplicate event suppression and consumer receipt rollback behavior.
asi.validation: Repository correctness checks passed.

description: Complete ADR-0033 atomic order cancellation and fulfillment workflows.

asi.hypothesis: The stored successful confirmation result is sufficient to coordinate cancellation/fulfillment without adding new tables or expanding Sales status.
asi.result: Process now persists idempotent cancellation/fulfillment runs, invokes only public owner commands, appends Process lifecycle events/jobs, and preserves atomic rollback when fulfilled reservations block cancellation.
asi.validation: 116 tests plus type, contract, boundary, and API checks passed.
asi.deliberate_scope: Sales order remains confirmed after fulfillment; Inventory owns the fulfilled reservation fact, while a later Sales fulfillment status requires a separate owner decision.

description: Reconciled P3 readiness and retired the legacy Process outbox, but snapshot merge produced invalid JSON.

asi.hypothesis: Final documentation, catalog semantics, and fail-closed legacy outbox retirement close the last readiness gate.
asi.rollback_reason: The custom migration snapshot was corrupted by a compacted jq output containing an ellipsis marker, so migration integrity tests failed.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply the final changes, generate a clean temporary current-schema snapshot, and merge JSON using a small Deno script or direct file processing that cannot compact output; validate JSON before running checks.
asi.important_changes_to_reapply: ADR-0038; current-vs-target messaging architecture; P3 bounded READY and two Level 3 slices; catalog preconditions/effects/delivery/sensitivity; fail-closed legacy Process outbox migration.

description: Finalize bounded P3 readiness, Level 3 catalog slices, and safe retirement of the legacy Process outbox.

asi.hypothesis: Explicit catalog semantics, truthful current-vs-target messaging docs, and a fail-closed ownership migration complete P3 without overclaiming PgQue or Process Studio.
asi.result: P3 is READY for the bounded PostgreSQL-internal baseline; inventory.stock.adjust v1 and accounting.revenue.post v1 are documented Level 3 slices; Process outbox retirement refuses non-empty legacy data.
asi.validation: All seven readiness gates and repository correctness checks passed.
asi.remaining_gates: PgQue activation, external connectors, Process aggregation/release persistence, Process IR/runtime/event waits, and deployment retention policy remain deliberately outside this readiness claim.

name: Harden P3 full-repository validation and canonical consistency

asi.hypothesis: Gate 7 should require formatting, linting, skills, boundary, contract, and type checks rather than type checking alone.
asi.rollback_reason: The tightened benchmark exposed two unformatted Party files and twelve immutable generated migration snapshots without trailing newlines.
asi.next_action_hint: Exclude immutable Drizzle snapshot artifacts from Deno formatting, format the two Party source/test files, then reconcile the canonical documentation contradictions found by final audit.

description: Make the final P3 gate require full validation and remove unsafe Accounting action-catalog overclaims.

asi.hypothesis: Full repository validation plus truthful catalog release state will close the hardened P3 gate without weakening domain behavior.
asi.result: Formatting, lint, type, skill, boundary, and contract checks pass; immutable Drizzle snapshots are excluded from formatting; Accounting retains its PUBLIC owner event but its caller-supplied-amount action is no longer catalog-released.
asi.validation: All seven hardened readiness gates passed, including the complete AGENTS validation portfolio.
asi.architecture_reconciliation: Corrected Sales lifecycle, Messaging outbox ownership, repository/package inventory, PostgreSQL schema registry, and Level 3 roadmap claims.

name: Resolve final P3 ADR and roadmap contradictions

description: Baseline the final ADR supersession and roadmap consistency checks with the full 117-test suite.

asi.hypothesis: A final canonical audit should require ADR-0033 to point to ADR-0038 and the Sales roadmap to distinguish owner state from coordinated fulfillment.
asi.result: All mechanical checks and 117 tests pass; one documentation consistency gate remains.
asi.next_action_hint: Annotate ADR-0033's partial supersession and update the Sales maturity row without rewriting the historical decision.

description: Reconcile ADR-0033's partial supersession and the Sales fulfillment roadmap boundary.

asi.hypothesis: Explicit supersession metadata and owner/coordinator wording remove the last canonical contradiction without changing accepted lifecycle semantics.
asi.result: ADR-0033 now points to ADR-0038 for outbox ownership while preserving its historical text, and Sales maturity distinguishes order state ownership from Process-coordinated Inventory fulfillment.
asi.validation: All seven gates, full formatting/lint/type/boundary/contract checks, and all 117 tests passed.

name: Resolve remaining Process Studio delivery wording

description: Baseline the remaining Process Studio event-delivery wording against the current Messaging implementation.

asi.hypothesis: ADR-0018 should distinguish the current Messaging outbox from the gated future PgQue adapter.
asi.result: All code and validation checks pass; one historical Process Studio wording gate remains.
asi.next_action_hint: Update ADR-0018's current-state context and delivery sentence while preserving PgQue as the selected future fan-out adapter.

description: Clarify current Messaging delivery and gated future PgQue fan-out in ADR-0018.

asi.hypothesis: Updating the Process Studio ADR's delivery wording removes the last current-vs-target contradiction without changing the accepted catalog decision.
asi.result: ADR-0018 now identifies Messaging outbox/receipts as current delivery and PgQue as the selected future adapter after activation gates.
asi.validation: All seven gates, full validation checks, and all 117 tests passed.

description: Re-run the fully hardened P3 portfolio after targeted messaging, lifecycle, migration, catalog, and canonical-document audits.

asi.hypothesis: A final independent audit and repeat run may expose another in-scope readiness defect.
asi.rollback_reason: No primary improvement was possible: all seven hardened gates and all 117 tests remained green, and no additional material in-scope defect was found.
asi.next_action_hint: Stop this bounded P3 objective; remaining ideas require PgQue activation, a second Level 3 action provider, Accounting amount provenance, external connectors, or Process Studio runtime work, all outside the current scope.

name: Add Sales order confirmation as the second Level 3 provider

description: Add Sales order confirmation as the second Level 3 action provider with atomic owner event publication.

asi.hypothesis: Sales order confirmation already has owner-derived totals, authorization, idempotency, and invalid-state semantics, so adding atomic owner event publication and catalog metadata is the smallest genuine second Level 3 slice.
asi.rollback_reason: The experiment command timed out at 60 seconds while the full validation portfolio was still running; focused type, boundary, and all 117 tests had passed before the timed run.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply the patch and rerun with a timeout above the observed full validation duration; do not change implementation solely to satisfy timing.

description: Publish Sales order confirmation as the second genuine Level 3 action/event slice.

asi.hypothesis: Sales order confirmation already owns server-derived totals, authorization, idempotency, and invalid-state semantics, so atomic owner event publication and catalog metadata provide the smallest safe second Level 3 provider.
asi.result: Sales confirm now carries distinct execution metadata, atomically emits sales.order.confirmed, rolls back when append fails, and is registered as a PUBLIC v1 action/event pair; Process forwards its metadata and catalog roadmaps now show two Level 3 domains.
asi.validation: All eight readiness gates passed; formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and all 117 tests passed. The first timed attempt was retried unchanged with a sufficient timeout.

description: Strengthen Sales confirmation rollback proof through successful same-key recovery.

asi.hypothesis: A failed atomic Sales confirmation must leave status, confirmed timestamp, idempotency key, and outbox untouched, then permit a successful retry with the same key.
asi.rollback_reason: The PostgreSQL client's RowList metadata made a whole-array deepStrictEqual type-invalid even though the intended assertions were sound.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply the proof using field-by-field assertions on rollbackRows[0], then confirm a same-key retry commits exactly one event.

description: Prove failed Sales confirmation is cleanly retriable with the same idempotency key.

asi.hypothesis: Field-level rollback assertions plus a successful same-key retry prove the atomic confirmation boundary is recoverable, not merely rolled back.
asi.rollback_reason: Behavior and all validation passed, but the new readiness gate searched for object-literal null assertions while the type-correct test used assert.isNull, so the primary metric did not improve.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain the behavioral test and make the gate recognize the actual field-level assertions rather than requiring a specific assertion representation.

description: Prove Sales confirmation rollback clears all confirmation state and permits same-key recovery.

asi.hypothesis: A failed atomic Sales confirmation must leave status, confirmed timestamp, idempotency key, and outbox untouched, then permit a successful retry with the same key.
asi.result: The PostgreSQL test now verifies all persisted confirmation fields remain clean after append failure and that retrying the same idempotency key confirms the order with exactly one owner event.
asi.validation: All nine readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 117-test portfolio passed.

description: Decouple Sales confirmation event identity from the Sales order aggregate identity.

asi.hypothesis: A domain event occurrence needs its own UUID rather than reusing the order aggregate ID, otherwise later Sales events for the same order would collide with the tenant-scoped outbox primary key.
asi.result: Both production and test Sales services now generate a distinct event ID; PostgreSQL proofs correlate through aggregate_type and aggregate_id while explicitly verifying the event ID differs from the order ID.
asi.validation: All ten readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 117-test portfolio passed.

description: Give Inventory and Accounting owner events distinct occurrence identities.

asi.hypothesis: Inventory and Accounting event occurrences should not reuse correction or journal aggregate IDs, matching the envelope's distinct event identity and avoiding future same-aggregate event collisions.
asi.result: Both production and test services now generate independent event UUIDs while retaining correction/journal IDs as aggregate IDs and payload correlation; unit and PostgreSQL tests explicitly prove the identities differ.
asi.validation: All eleven readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 117-test portfolio passed.

description: Enforce UUID identity at all PUBLIC domain-event payload boundaries.

asi.hypothesis: PUBLIC event payload identifiers should validate as UUIDs, matching persisted domain identities and preventing malformed candidate events from entering catalog consumers.
asi.result: Inventory correction, Accounting revenue, and Sales confirmation payload schemas now validate their domain identifiers as UUIDs; compatibility fixtures use valid UUIDs.
asi.validation: All twelve readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 117-test portfolio passed.

description: Enforce owner namespaces for every typed domain-event declaration.

asi.hypothesis: A domain-owned event declaration must use its owning domain as the event-type namespace, preventing catalog metadata from assigning business meaning to the wrong owner.
asi.result: Catalog compatibility now rejects event IDs that do not begin with the declared owning domain namespace across Inventory, Accounting, and Sales contributors.
asi.validation: All thirteen readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 117-test portfolio passed.

description: Bind every typed domain action identity to its authorization capability identity.

asi.hypothesis: A catalog action must authorize the capability with the same stable identifier; allowing action and capability IDs to diverge could protect a published business action with the wrong permission.
asi.result: Catalog compatibility now requires action.id to equal requiredCapability for both Inventory stock adjustment and Sales order confirmation providers.
asi.validation: All fourteen readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 117-test portfolio passed.

description: Validate typed event correlation and filter metadata as a coherent consumer contract.

asi.hypothesis: Event correlation fields must be nonempty, unique, and included in a duplicate-free filterable-field set so catalog consumers can reliably correlate and query candidates.
asi.rollback_reason: The implementation was semantically valid but failed the repository formatter because the one-line for loop requires braces.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply the assertions in formatter-compliant block form and rerun unchanged.

description: Validate typed event correlation and filter metadata as a coherent consumer contract.

asi.hypothesis: Event correlation fields must be nonempty, unique, and included in a duplicate-free filterable-field set so catalog consumers can reliably correlate and query candidates.
asi.result: Catalog compatibility now rejects empty or duplicate correlation metadata, duplicate filter metadata, and correlation fields that consumers cannot filter on.
asi.validation: All fifteen readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 117-test portfolio passed.

description: Validate every filterable event field against its declared payload schema.

asi.hypothesis: Catalog filter metadata must name real payload fields; otherwise consumers receive a published filter contract that cannot be evaluated against the event payload.
asi.rollback_reason: Behavior and all repository validation passed, but the readiness gate miscounted three helper calls as four by incorrectly assuming the helper declaration matched the call pattern.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply unchanged and correct the gate to require the three domain-event calls.

description: Validate every filterable event field against its declared payload schema.

asi.hypothesis: Catalog filter metadata must name real payload fields; otherwise consumers receive a published filter contract that cannot be evaluated against the event payload.
asi.result: Catalog compatibility now checks all Inventory, Accounting, and Sales filterable fields against their actual Struct schema fields; correlation fields are already required to be filterable.
asi.validation: All sixteen readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 117-test portfolio passed.

description: Prove duplicate-safe consumer completion under concurrent PostgreSQL delivery.

asi.hypothesis: Sequential duplicate tests do not prove the receipt race; two concurrent deliveries must commit exactly one local effect and receipt while classifying the other as duplicate.
asi.result: The PostgreSQL consumeOnce proof now races two deliveries of the same event and verifies one winner, one duplicate, one derived event, and one durable receipt.
asi.validation: All seventeen readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 117-test portfolio passed.

description: Prove the losing concurrent consumer rolls back a non-idempotent PostgreSQL-local mutation.

asi.hypothesis: The duplicate race must roll back a genuinely non-idempotent local mutation, because an idempotent derived-event append can mask a double execution defect.
asi.rollback_reason: The test imported the private messaging table, violating the repository rule that tests consume public contracts rather than persistence definitions.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply the same transactional race using the public Database service with test-only SQL, without importing the private table schema.

description: Prove the losing concurrent consumer rolls back a non-idempotent PostgreSQL-local mutation.

asi.hypothesis: The duplicate race must roll back a genuinely non-idempotent local mutation, because an idempotent derived-event append can mask a double execution defect.
asi.result: Two concurrent consumeOnce calls now race an increment inside the ambient transaction; the proof verifies one winner, one duplicate, one committed increment, and one receipt without importing private messaging tables.
asi.validation: All eighteen readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 118-test portfolio passed.

description: Prove a failed consumer can recover with the same receipt identity.

asi.hypothesis: Receipt rollback is incomplete evidence unless the same consumer and event can subsequently retry, commit its local effect, and record one completed receipt.
asi.result: The failed-consumer PostgreSQL proof now retries the same receipt identity after rollback and verifies one recovered derived event and one completed receipt.
asi.validation: All nineteen readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 118-test portfolio passed.

description: Prove transaction-aware event append is idempotent under concurrent retries.

asi.hypothesis: Sequential append replay does not prove the outbox uniqueness race; concurrent identical envelopes must converge on one stored event and the same returned envelope.
asi.result: The PostgreSQL messaging proof now races two identical append calls, verifies both return the same envelope, retains mismatch conflict behavior, and confirms one durable row.
asi.validation: All twenty readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 118-test portfolio passed.

description: Prove concurrent mismatched event envelopes fail with one typed conflict.

asi.hypothesis: Concurrent callers using the same event identity key with different envelopes must not both succeed; exactly one durable event and one typed idempotency conflict should result.
asi.result: The PostgreSQL messaging proof now races mismatched envelopes sharing one event type, version, and idempotency key, verifying one success, one EventIdempotencyConflict, and one outbox row.
asi.validation: All twenty-one readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 119-test portfolio passed.

description: Prove messaging event and idempotency identities remain tenant-scoped.

asi.hypothesis: Tenant-scoped primary and deduplication keys must allow identical event IDs and idempotency keys in different tenants without cross-tenant conflict or envelope leakage.
asi.result: The PostgreSQL messaging proof concurrently appends identical event, aggregate, and idempotency identities for two tenants, verifies distinct tenant envelopes, and confirms two durable rows.
asi.validation: All twenty-two readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 120-test portfolio passed.
asi.observation: Benchmark duration spiked to 527 seconds while correctness checks completed normally; no implementation change was made to optimize timing.

description: Prove cross-tenant consumer receipts fail without committing local effects.

asi.hypothesis: A consumer must not create a receipt for another tenant's event, and the foreign-key rejection must roll back any PostgreSQL-local effect attempted in the same transaction.
asi.result: The PostgreSQL messaging proof uses a tenant-mismatched receipt around a non-idempotent increment, verifies a stable DatabaseFailure, and confirms zero increments and zero receipts.
asi.validation: All twenty-three readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 121-test portfolio passed.
